lessons.title: Never have I seen...
lessons.goal_uz: Not only, Rarely, Under no circumstances, Had I known kabi inversiya tuzilmalari bilan fikrni kuchli va rasmiy ifodalaysiz.

words.ex: The city has seen unprecedented growth.

steps.title: A speech at graduation
steps.text: Never have I felt so proud to stand in front of a group of students. Four years ago, few of you could have imagined where you would be today. Not only have you completed one of the most demanding programmes in the country, but you have also done it during a period of unprecedented change. Rarely does a class face so many challenges — online lectures, closed libraries, uncertain futures — and still achieve such remarkable results. Had you given up in that difficult second year, none of us would be here celebrating. So, as you leave, remember this: under no circumstances should you stop asking questions. Only by staying curious will you continue to grow.
steps.uz: Hech qachon bir guruh talabalar oldida turib bunchalik faxrlanmaganman. To'rt yil oldin orangizdan kamdan-kam kishi bugun qayerda bo'lishini tasavvur qila olardi. Siz nafaqat mamlakatdagi eng og'ir dasturlardan birini tugatdingiz, balki buni misli ko'rilmagan o'zgarishlar davrida qildingiz. Kamdan-kam guruh shuncha qiyinchilikka — onlayn ma'ruzalar, yopiq kutubxonalar, noaniq kelajak — duch kelib, shunday ajoyib natijalarga erishadi. Agar o'sha qiyin ikkinchi kursda taslim bo'lganingizda, hech birimiz bu yerda nishonlamayotgan bo'lardik. Shuning uchun ketar ekansiz, buni yodda tuting: hech qanday holatda savol berishdan to'xtamang. Faqat qiziquvchan bo'lib qolsangizgina o'sishda davom etasiz.

steps.explain_uz: "Had you given up in that difficult second year..." — taslim bo'lishmagan.

steps.explain_uz: "under no circumstances should you stop asking questions".

steps.title_uz: Inversiya — ega va yordamchi fe'l o'rin almashadi
steps.body_uz:
Gap **inkor yoki cheklovchi ravish** bilan boshlansa, keyingi qism **savol tartibida** bo'ladi: **ravish + yordamchi fe'l + ega + fe'l**.
I have **never** seen... → **Never have I** seen...
He **rarely** calls. → **Rarely does he** call. (yordamchi fe'l yo'q bo'lsa — **do / does / did** qo'shiladi)
Asosiy iboralar: **Never / Rarely / Seldom** · **Not only ... but (also)** · **Under no circumstances** · **No sooner had ... than** · **Hardly / Scarcely had ... when** · **Only by / Only when / Only after** · **Little did I know**.
**if** siz shart: **Had I known** = If I had known · **Should you need** = If you need · **Were I you** = If I were you.
Xato: "Not only he arrived late..." — inversiya yo'q! To'g'ri: Not only **did he arrive** late...
Maslahat: IELTS Writing/Speaking'da 1–2 marta ishlating — ortiqchasi sun'iy eshitiladi.

steps.prompt_uz: Hayotingizdagi muhim voqea yoki yutuq haqida yozing (100+ so'z). Kamida 3 xil inversiya ishlating (Never have I..., Not only..., Little did I know..., Had I...).
steps.prompt: Describe an important moment or achievement in your life. Use at least three different inverted structures.
steps.example: The day I received my university acceptance letter is one I will never forget. Little did I know, when I first started learning English at the age of fifteen, that it would one day take me abroad. Not only did I have to prepare for IELTS, but I also had to write essays and attend an online interview. There were moments when I almost gave up. Had my teacher not encouraged me, I would probably have stopped after my first disappointing score. When the email finally arrived, I read it three times. Never have I felt such a mixture of relief and excitement. Only then did I realise how much those two years of hard work had been worth.

lessons.title: What really matters is...
lessons.title_uz: Cleft sentences: diqqatni bir joyga qaratish
lessons.goal_uz: "What I need is...", "It was ... that..." tuzilmalari bilan gapdagi eng muhim qismni ajratib ko'rsatasiz — Speaking'da ravonlik va aniqlik uchun.

words.ex: Sleep is crucial for memory.
Waiting in long queues is frustrating.

She pointed out a mistake in my essay.

steps.title: Speaking Part 3: learning languages
steps.context_uz: IELTS imtihonchisi nomzoddan til o'rganish haqida chuqurroq so'rayapti.

lines.en: What do you think is the most important factor in learning a language?
lines.uz: Sizningcha, til o'rganishda eng muhim omil nima?

lines.en: Well, what most people assume is that talent matters most. But what really makes the difference, in my view, is consistency.
lines.uz: Ko'pchilik iste'dod eng muhim deb o'ylaydi. Lekin menimcha, haqiqiy farqni izchillik yaratadi.

lines.en: Sure. It was my cousin who taught me this. She studied for just twenty minutes a day, but she never skipped a day. What impressed me was that she reached band seven in a year.
lines.uz: Albatta. Buni menga xolamning qizi o'rgatgan. U kuniga atigi yigirma daqiqa o'qirdi, lekin bir kunni ham qoldirmasdi. Meni hayratga solgani — u bir yilda 7 ballga erishdi.

lines.en: The thing about motivation is that it comes and goes. What keeps you going on difficult days is habit, not feelings.
lines.uz: Motivatsiyaning o'ziga xosligi shundaki, u keladi-yu ketadi. Qiyin kunlarda sizni olg'a yetaklaydigan narsa — his-tuyg'u emas, odat.

steps.q: According to the candidate, what matters most?
steps.explain_uz: "what really makes the difference... is consistency".

steps.q: Why does the candidate mention their cousin?
options: As an example of consistent study
Because she studied for hours every day
steps.explain_uz: Kuniga 20 daqiqa, lekin har kuni — izchillik misoli.

steps.body_uz:
Oddiy gapni ikki qismga bo'lib, **eng muhim ma'lumotni** ajratib ko'rsatamiz.
**1. What-cleft**: **What + ega + fe'l + is/was + urg'uli qism**.
I need a holiday. → **What I need is** a holiday.
Consistency makes the difference. → **What makes the difference is** consistency.
**2. It-cleft**: **It is/was + urg'uli qism + that/who + qolgan qism**.
My cousin taught me this. → **It was my cousin who** taught me this.
I met her in Bukhara. → **It was in Bukhara that** I met her.
**3. Boshqa shakllar**: **The thing (that) I like is...** · **The reason why... is that...** · **All I want is...** · **What happened was (that)...**
Harakatga urg'u: **What I did was (to)** + fe'l — What I did was (to) call my teacher. Voqeaga urg'u: **What happened was (that)** I lost my keys.
Speaking'da bu tuzilmalar o'ylash uchun tabiiy vaqt beradi va Fluency/Grammar ballini oshiradi.

steps.prompt_uz: Speaking Part 3 savoliga yozma javob bering (100+ so'z): "What makes a good teacher?" Kamida 3 ta cleft sentence ishlating.
steps.prompt: What makes a good teacher? Answer as you would in Speaking Part 3, using at least three cleft sentences.
steps.example: That's an interesting question. What many people think is that a good teacher simply needs deep knowledge of their subject. Knowledge is obviously important, but what really distinguishes a great teacher, in my opinion, is the ability to spark curiosity. It was my history teacher at school who showed me this. She rarely lectured; instead, she asked questions that made us argue and think. The reason why her lessons stayed with me is that she treated us as people with ideas, not as empty containers. All a student really needs, I think, is someone who believes they can improve.

lessons.title: The growth of cities
lessons.goal_uz: Fe'l va sifatlarni otga aylantirib (grow → growth), Writing Task 2 gaplarini qisqa, aniq va akademik qilasiz.

words.ex: Rapid urbanisation creates new problems.
Our reliance on cars is increasing.
There has been a deterioration in air quality.
The availability of cheap flights has changed tourism.
The implementation of the new law took two years.
Smoking is detrimental to health.
Pollution is a consequence of rapid growth.
The accessibility of online courses has improved.

steps.title: Two versions of the same paragraph
steps.text:
Version A (B1): Cities are growing very fast, and because of this, people are using cars more and more. When more people drive, the air gets worse, and many people get ill because they breathe dirty air.

Version B (C1): The rapid growth of cities has led to an increasing reliance on private vehicles. This rise in car use has, in turn, resulted in a serious deterioration in air quality, with a corresponding increase in respiratory illness among urban residents.
steps.uz:
A varianti (B1): Shaharlar juda tez o'smoqda va shu sababli odamlar mashinadan tobora ko'proq foydalanmoqda. Ko'proq odam mashina haydasa, havo yomonlashadi va ko'p odamlar iflos havodan nafas olgani uchun kasal bo'ladi.

B varianti (C1): Shaharlarning tez o'sishi shaxsiy transport vositalariga tayanishning ortishiga olib keldi. Avtomobildan foydalanishning bu o'sishi, o'z navbatida, havo sifatining jiddiy yomonlashuviga va shu bilan birga shahar aholisi orasida nafas yo'li kasalliklarining ko'payishiga sabab bo'ldi.

steps.q: What is the main difference between Version A and Version B?
options: B expresses the same ideas using nouns instead of verbs.
B is longer and more informal.
steps.explain_uz: G'oya bir xil — B'da fe'llar otlarga aylangan: growing → **growth**, gets worse → **deterioration**.

steps.q: Which phrase in Version B replaces "people are using cars more and more"?
options: an increasing reliance on private vehicles

steps.body_uz:
Akademik ingliz tilida harakat ko'pincha **ot** bilan ifodalanadi. Bu gapni qisqa, ob'ektiv va zich qiladi.
**Fe'l → ot**: grow → **growth** · increase → **an increase** · rely on → **reliance on** · develop → **development** · fail → **failure** · decide → **decision** · implement → **implementation**
**Sifat → ot**: available → **availability** · important → **importance** · difficult → **difficulty** · accessible → **accessibility**
Tuzilma: **sifat + ot + of + ot**: Prices rose sharply. → **a sharp rise in prices**. The government decided quickly. → **the government's swift decision**.
Ot guruhi gapning **egasi** bo'ladi va keyin bog'lovchi fe'l keladi: **The rapid growth of cities has led to...** / **...has resulted in...** / **...is a major cause of...**
Ehtiyot bo'ling: har bir gapni nominalizatsiya qilmang — 1–2 abzatsda bir necha marta yetarli, aks holda matn og'ir o'qiladi.

examples.en: Unemployment rose sharply. → There was a sharp rise in unemployment.
People can easily access the internet. → The easy accessibility of the internet...
The government failed to act, which caused the crisis. → The government's failure to act caused the crisis.
examples.uz: Hukumatning harakat qilmagani inqirozga sabab bo'ldi.

examples.en: The introduction of fees has reduced the number of applicants.
examples.uz: To'lovlarning joriy etilishi abituriyentlar sonini kamaytirdi.

options: Because people rely on phones, they sleep less.
Reliance on smartphones has been linked to reduced sleep.
People use phones a lot so they don't sleep.
steps.explain_uz: Ot guruhi (**Reliance on smartphones**) ega bo'lgan, ob'ektiv uslub.

steps.prompt_uz: Quyidagi oddiy matnni nominalizatsiya yordamida akademik uslubda qayta yozing (80+ so'z): "Lots of young people are moving to big cities because they want jobs. Because of this, villages are getting smaller and older people live alone. Also, cities are getting very crowded and houses cost a lot."
steps.prompt: Rewrite the paragraph in an academic style using nominalisation.
steps.example: The migration of young people to large cities in search of employment has had significant consequences for both rural and urban areas. In the countryside, this movement has resulted in a steady decline in village populations and an increase in the number of elderly people living alone. In cities, meanwhile, the rapid growth of the population has led to severe overcrowding and a sharp rise in the cost of housing. The lack of affordable accommodation is now a major concern for many urban residents.
